title: Entanglement-Assisted Timing Optimization for Discriminating Amplitude-Damping Dynamics
authors: Massimiliano F. Sacchi, Milajiguli Rexiti, Stefano Mancini
abstract: We analyze minimum-error discrimination of two qubit dynamical processes generated by phase-covariant amplitude-damping Lindbladians in a single-use scenario. The optimization involves both the input probe, possibly entangled with an isolated ancilla, and the interrogation time. For unassisted probes we obtain a closed expression for the optimal trace-norm distinguishability at fixed time, with distinct interior and boundary branches. For entanglement-assisted probes, the common phase covariance of the two channels reduces the diamond-norm optimization to a one-parameter Schmidt family. The resulting formula gives transparent sufficient conditions for fixed-time entanglement advantage and separates this local advantage from advantage after global optimization over time. We exhibit examples in which the best unassisted strategy is approached only asymptotically, whereas an entangled probe achieves a strictly smaller error probability at finite time.
summary: This paper analyzes how to best distinguish between two noisy qubit dynamics (amplitude-damping channels) by optimizing both the input probe state and the measurement time. It rigorously proves that utilizing initial entanglement can yield a measurable, finite-time advantage over any strategy using only unentangled probes. This highlights the practical utility of quantum resources in characterizing open quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the minimum-error discrimination of two distinct qubit dynamical processes generated by phase-covariant amplitude-damping Lindbladians.
main_result: Entanglement assistance can provide a strictly smaller error probability at finite time compared to the best unassisted strategy, and this advantage can persist even when considering global optimization over interrogation time.
method: The authors use quantum information theory tools, comparing trace-norm distinguishability (unassisted) against diamond-norm distinguishability (entangled), optimizing over input states and interrogation time $t$.
model_or_system: The system involves two qubits undergoing dynamics governed by a phase-covariant amplitude-damping Lindbladian master equation. The evolution is analyzed via its effect on the Bloch vector.
key_observables: Trace-norm distinguishability ($D_{	ext{sep}}(t)$) and diamond-norm distinguishability ($D_{	ext{ent}}(t)$), which quantify the minimum error probability for discrimination.
important_parameters: Interrogation time ($t$), damping rates ($\gamma_\pm, \gamma_z$), and the entanglement parameterization via a one-parameter Schmidt family.
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on single-use scenarios and distinguishes between fixed-time advantages and globally optimized timing advantages over $t$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate numerical examples demonstrating finite-time advantages ($e^*_E < p^*_E$) where the entangled strategy outperforms the unassisted one, particularly in regimes governed by specific conditions on damping rates.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general framework for discrimination using both unassisted and entanglement-assisted measures. It then derives explicit formulas for fixed time $t$ based on different optimal input state branches (interior vs. boundary). Finally, it compares the optimized results to show when and how entanglement provides a measurable advantage over classical or unassisted quantum measurements.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes the boundaries of quantum process tomography and channel discrimination by quantifying the precise resource benefit provided by initial entanglement in open quantum system settings.
